# googleworkspace_chrome_policy_group_priority_ordering (Resource)

Chrome Policy Group Priority Ordering resource in the Terraform Googleworkspace provider. This resource manages the priority order of the groups that set a Chrome policy for an app: when groups set different values, the value of the group that is first in `group_ids` applies. The API supports an ordering only for the policies of an app: `policy_target_key` must have the app in `additional_target_key_names`. The API has no delete operation for an ordering, so destroying this resource only removes it from the Terraform state, and the ordering stays in Google Workspace. Chrome Policy Schema resides under the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chrome.management.policy` client scope.

Each write must include every group that currently sets the policy for the app. A list without one of these groups is an error of the API.

* To add a group, add its `googleworkspace_chrome_group_policy` and add the group to `group_ids` in the same apply. Set `depends_on` to the group policies, so that the group policy is created before the ordering is written.
* To remove a group, use two applies. First remove the `googleworkspace_chrome_group_policy` of the group from the configuration and from `depends_on`, keep the group in `group_ids`, and apply. Because `group_ids` does not change, this apply only destroys the group policy. Then remove the group from `group_ids` and apply again. If the group is the last group in `group_ids`, remove the ordering resource from the configuration instead: when no group sets the policy, the next refresh removes the ordering from state, and `group_ids` needs at least one group. In one apply, Terraform writes the ordering before it destroys the group policy, so the write leaves out a group that still sets the policy, and the API rejects it. This order follows the API rule above, and is not tested against the live API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

resource "googleworkspace_group" "security" {
  email = "chrome-security@example.com"
}

resource "googleworkspace_group" "pilot" {
  email = "chrome-pilot@example.com"
}

# Both groups set the policy of an app. The value of the first group in group_ids applies to users in both groups.
resource "googleworkspace_chrome_group_policy" "security" {
  group_id = googleworkspace_group.security.id
  additional_target_keys {
    target_key   = "app_id"
    target_value = "chrome:ghbmnnjooekpmoecnnnilnnbdlolhkhi"
  }
  policies {
    schema_name = "chrome.users.apps.InstallType"
    schema_values = {
      appInstallType = jsonencode("BLOCKED")
    }
  }
}

resource "googleworkspace_chrome_group_policy" "pilot" {
  group_id = googleworkspace_group.pilot.id
  additional_target_keys {
    target_key   = "app_id"
    target_value = "chrome:ghbmnnjooekpmoecnnnilnnbdlolhkhi"
  }
  policies {
    schema_name = "chrome.users.apps.InstallType"
    schema_values = {
      appInstallType = jsonencode("FORCED")
    }
  }
}

resource "googleworkspace_chrome_policy_group_priority_ordering" "docs_offline" {
  policy_namespace = "chrome.users.apps"

  policy_target_key {
    additional_target_key_names = {
      app_id = "chrome:ghbmnnjooekpmoecnnnilnnbdlolhkhi"
    }
  }

  # Highest priority first. List every group that sets the policy for the app: the API rejects a partial list.
  group_ids = [
    googleworkspace_group.security.id,
    googleworkspace_group.pilot.id,
  ]

  depends_on = [
    googleworkspace_chrome_group_policy.security,
    googleworkspace_chrome_group_policy.pilot,
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `group_ids` (List of String) The IDs of the groups, in priority order: the policy value of a group overrides the values of the groups after it. The API requires every group that currently sets the policy for the app: a list without one of them is an error of the API, not drift. See the description of the resource to add or remove a group.
- `policy_target_key` (Block List, Min: 1, Max: 1) The target of the ordering. The API requires the app in `additional_target_key_names`, for example `app_id = "chrome:<extension ID>"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--policy_target_key))

### Optional

- `policy_namespace` (String) The namespace of the policy type, for example `chrome.users.apps` for the policies of an app. Set either `policy_schema` or `policy_namespace`.
- `policy_schema` (String) The full qualified name of the policy schema, for example `chrome.users.apps.InstallType`. Set either `policy_schema` or `policy_namespace`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--policy_target_key"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policy_target_key`

Required:

- `additional_target_key_names` (Map of String) A map of additional target key names to their values, for example `{ app_id = "chrome:<extension ID>" }`. The API requires the app.

Optional:

- `target_resource` (String) The target resource. The examples of the API leave it empty and set only the app in `additional_target_key_names`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

# <policy_schema>:<target_resource>:<key>=<value>[+<key>=<value>...]
terraform import googleworkspace_chrome_policy_group_priority_ordering.install_type chrome.users.apps.InstallType::app_id=chrome:ghbmnnjooekpmoecnnnilnnbdlolhkhi

# namespace=<policy_namespace>:<target_resource>:<key>=<value>[+<key>=<value>...]
terraform import googleworkspace_chrome_policy_group_priority_ordering.docs_offline namespace=chrome.users.apps::app_id=chrome:ghbmnnjooekpmoecnnnilnnbdlolhkhi
```
